claims.event: Called the Iron Spear, mustered followers with his brother Fu, married Lady Yang, and took Juzhou for the Song.
Rose at Tai-an and raided Zibo and Yizhou until his death.
Succeeded Erzu, failed to take Yizhou, and was executed by Ting.
Joined Huo Yi and later submitted to Li Quan.

Raided Ju and Mi, was defeated by Wanyan Ting, was killed by a boatman, and had intended to submit to the Song.
Served as a strategist of Yang Aner.
Served as a strategist of Yang Aner.
Commanded for his nephew Yang Aner, rallied troops around the Fourth Lady, and encamped at Gushang.

Jin commissioner who defeated Aner and Quan, executed Huo Yi, and was originally named Li Ercuo.
Served as administrative officer under Wanyan Ting; he was Aruda.
Nephew of Aner who styled himself the Ninth Great King and neglected military affairs.
Fierce rider and archer called Auntie, who married Li Quan.
Charged Quan with his spear but was held back; nicknamed Rival to Zhang Fei.
Zhang Hui was nicknamed his rival.
Smuggled rice at Shanyang, persuaded Chunzhi to relax the Huai crossing ban, and raised loyalist militia.
Paid in jade goods, strengthened river defenses, and reported that the Central Plains could be recovered.
Served Liu You, conveyed the wish of northern heroes to submit, and attached Quan to Zhongjiao.
Great knight whose household retainer was Ji Xian.
Ordered stronger river defenses and secretly received the northern loyalists.
Ordered Chunzhi to strengthen river defenses.
Raised loyalist militia and took Haizhou with Quan.
Captured when Quan stormed Juzhou.
Mindful of Kaixi, secretly ordered the northern loyalists received as the Loyalist Army.
Converged on Lianshui with ten thousand men.
Converged on Lianshui with Ma Liang.
Converged on Lianshui with Ma Liang.

label.en: Deputy Commander of the Wufeng Army

claims.event: Captured Huang Gui, ambushed the Jin at Wokou, became sworn brother of Zhang Lin, claimed a false reward, and withdrew from Sizhou.
Pleaded with Bing for rations and advanced to Tianchang.
Richly rewarded Quan and his subordinates.
Captured at Mizhou and sent in chains to Chucheng.
Could not feed the submitters, put Shi Gui in charge, and sent Quan to reason with him.
Seized grain boats and raided across the Huai; the officers sent against him would not fight.
Was defeated at Nandu Gate.
Met Shi Gui and refused to fight him.
Met Shi Gui and refused to fight him.
Garrisoned Hao and lost three thousand horsemen.
Suffered losses against the Jin.
Ambushed by Quan while crossing; thousands of his men drowned.
Joined Quan in ambushing the Jin at Wokou.
Defeated at Huabihu and lost his gold plaque, yet was not in fact killed.
Enfeoffed as Lady Lingren when Quan was promoted.
Submitted twelve prefectures, swore brotherhood with Quan, and was appointed Jingdong commissioner.
Composed the memorial of submission.
Was appointed controller when Quan was promoted and the army moved to Chuzhou.
Was appointed controller alongside Liu Qingfu when the army moved to Chuzhou.
Promised rewards for killing Jin royals and memorialized for Quan's reward.
Feasted Quan and the generals at Xuyi.
Offered three thousand long-spear troops to follow Quan.
Offered three thousand long-spear troops to follow Quan.

label.en: Jingdong Pacification Commissioner and Overall Commander

claims.event: Challenged battle at Dongping, retreated to Changqing, had Xian slandered, deceived She over the rolls, fled Sizhou, and received Zhang Hui.
Sought to submit and presented nine prefectures through Zhao Gong.
Made a pact with Yan Shi and urged Quan to seize Dongping.
Joined Quan against Dongping and returned to Qingzhou.
Held Dongping against Quan.
Killed in the defeat before Dongping.
Rivaled Quan in prestige and died after being slandered.
Enlisted by Quan to slander Xian.
Sent to command the army of Xian but was rejected.
Refused Chen Xuan, feigned acceptance of a seal, and was killed by Gui.
Refused Chen Xuan and was taken by Gui to the Mongols.
Refused Chen Xuan and was taken by Gui to the Mongols.
Refused to accept Chen Xuan and welcomed Shi Gui.
Refused to accept Chen Xuan and welcomed Shi Gui.
Refused to accept Chen Xuan and welcomed Shi Gui.
Became commander of the partisans, defied orders, and went over to the Mongols.
Taken by Gui to submit to the Mongols.
Proposed by She to verify phantom rolls.
Proposed by Quan as overall commander at Yangzhou.
Met Quan with boats and staged a musical feast.
Hosted Quan and refused him a courtesan.
Stocked western Sizhou from Xuyi and retook it.
Killed when Quan was routed at western Sizhou.
Intercepted the Jin at Tianchang.
Intercepted the Jin at Tianchang with his brother.
Defeated Quan often but surrendered to him and received his own army.
Profited from trade at Jiaoxi, entered Qingzhou, took over the loyalist rolls, quarreled with Xu Guo over the bow, then feigned deference.
Held Jiaoxi, extorted Lin over salt, and fled to Chuzhou.
Burdened by Fu, submitted to the Mongols, and fled Qingzhou.
Persuaded Lin to submit to the Mongols.
Sent to comfort Lin and killed on the road by Quan.
Sent to comfort Lin with Wang Yi and killed on return.
Cleared the road for She, was rebuffed by Guo, and prepared against a plot.
Commanded eight thousand Zhenjiang troops in the city.
Commanded loyalists west of the city and wept when leaving Guo.
Commanded loyalists and was praised by Quan.
Commanded five thousand at Huaiyin.
Commanded five thousand at Huaiyin with Wang Hui.
Bribed by Quan as a Zhenjiang controller.
Bribed by Quan as a Zhenjiang controller.
Approved the new rolls proposed by Quan.
Warned of rebellion, suppressed the northern army, demanded Quan's bow, and held a grand review.
Memorialized that Guo was unfit to command Huai.
Sent Quan a memorial praising Guo.
Offered to submit, imprisoned Wang Xier, and repelled Quan at Pi.
Obtained the letter of Li Ercuo and reported it.
Sent with two thousand men and imprisoned by Ercuo.
Probed Guo's intent and was humiliated by Mengxian.
Made Qingfu bow from behind a screen.
Asked that Zhao Bangyong be sent to Shandong.

label.en: Military Governor of the Zhaoxin Army

claims.event: Resolved to move against Guo and sent Qingfu to Chuzhou.
Raised troops and salt smugglers claiming to enthrone the Prince of Ji.
Took up arms with his cousin Pan Fu.
Dismissed warnings, was wounded by mutineers, and hanged himself on the road.
Plotted the mutiny, killed Mengxian, and sent Wenxin to Yangzhou.
Kept a pretended imperial clansman and arranged support from Xuyi.
Conspired to seize Yangzhou, feigned wounds, and withdrew to Chuzhou.
Reported the plot to Guo and then warned Qingfu.
Brought into the city and rewarded the troops.
Killed by Qingfu in revenge for the screen insult.
Trusted by Guo but defected to the rebels.
Trusted by Guo but defected to the rebels.
Trusted by Guo but defected to the rebels.
Refused to yield and fought the rebels.
Refused to yield and fought the rebels.
Refused to yield and killed the rebel officer Ma Liang.
Refused to yield and fought the rebels.
Refused to yield and fought the rebels.
Killed by Shen Xing in the alley fighting.
Warned the rebels that the court would not spare them.
Debated receiving Wenxin, hesitated to kill him, and was forced to reward his men.
Lured Wenxin into Yangzhou and talked him down at Pingshan Hall.
Burst into the prefectural hall, held Wang Tong, and withdrew to Chuzhou.
Harbored rebellious designs but was bought off.
Bribed Xia Quan and sent Bian Zheng to watch him.
Returned to Yangzhou and spread false reports of rebellion.
Decided to endure the insult for the moment and plan a response later.
Sent to placate Quan, raised Liu Quan, secretly protected Shixiong, and let Quan go unchecked.
Claimed command after Guo died, was wounded by Shi Qing, murdered Mengyu, and was routed by Yibin.
Rescued Quan, rewarded a document thief, and was beaten relieving Quan.
Swore revenge, defeated Quan, won over Wu Xian, and died fighting the Mongols.
His stolen papers revealed a court order to plot against Quan.
Summoned by Yibin as a southerner to proclaim the cause.
Recovered the commissioner seal and pleaded for action against the rebels.
Bowed to Xiji, plotted over vouchers, and wished to go north.
Caught under a false name and executed at the capital.
Seized Pan Ren and sent him to the capital.
Disguised men as Jin troops and ambushed Quan.
Urged pursuit of the northern army and refused to yield to Quan.
Made a controller in secret and fought his way to Yangzhou.
Imprisoned by Xiji at Chuzhou when Xiji and Quan still cooperated, so the rebels still showed fear.
Driven out of Chuzhou by Xiji when Xiji and Quan still cooperated, so the rebels still showed fear.
Drank with Quan and reported his officers talk of revolt.
Called Benefactor Hall and paid off Liu Quan.
Exposed as an informer and murdered by Quan outside the city.
Jin general who surrendered to Yibin.
Received a letter from Yibin urging action against Quan.
Returned to Quan after Yibin died.

label.en: Prefect and Judicial Intendant of Yangzhou

claims.event: Won over Shi Qing, went to Shandong, was besieged at Qingzhou, and stayed while Fu left.
Submitted to Quan after Yibin died, moved to Huaiyin, and then into Chuzhou.
His death led Shi Qing to submit to Quan.
Feasted Qing, temporized timidly, and was recalled.
Retired on temple stipend from Yangzhou.
Became prefect of Yangzhou and acting judicial intendant.
Urged Quan to flee, left the besieged city, and failed to send relief.
Sought command, reached Chuzhou with Zhenjiang troops, and was overtaken by events.
Praised Zhuo at court, replaced him at Xuyi, and goaded Xia Quan.
Kept at Xuyi, marched into Chuzhou, and paraded his troops before the rebels.
Bribed Xia Quan to ease the pressure on Chuzhou.
